setup_summary.text: NVIDIA reports fiscal Q3 2027 on 2026-11-17 after the close. Q2 (July quarter) revenue was $96.22B, up 105.9% YoY, with diluted EPS of $2.46 (+127.8%) and a 66.2% operating margin.

Q2 growth was led by ACIE (AI Clouds, Industrial & Enterprise) at $40.3B (+25% QoQ, +138% YoY). Hyperscale was $48.7B (+13% QoQ). Data Center in total was $89.0B (+18% QoQ). Management guided Q3 sequential growth to come mainly from ACIE.

Q3 guidance is revenue of $108B ±2% (about $105.8B–$110.2B), GAAP and non-GAAP gross margin of 74% ±50bp, and GAAP/non-GAAP opex of about $9.2B/$9.0B. The guide assumes no China data center compute revenue. Vera Rubin should be about 20% of Data Center revenue.

Consensus for Q3 is revenue of $111.36B and EPS of $2.53. Revenue consensus is about 3% above the guide midpoint and above the top of the guided range. That implies +95% YoY revenue growth, against +89% at the guide midpoint. NVIDIA has beaten 4 of the last 4 quarters, with an average surprise of +3.4%.

The Q2 print did not show operating leverage in EPS. Operating income rose 19% QoQ, but net income rose only 2% and EPS 3%. The 10-Q shows $7.77B of equity-security gains in Q2, about 11% of pre-tax income, after first-half gains of $23.7B. That puts Q1 gains at roughly $15.9B. EPS comparisons therefore depend heavily on non-operating marks. A preview cites Q2 adjusted EPS of $2.22 against GAAP $2.46.

Management gave a first-ever full-year preliminary outlook: about +70% FY2028 revenue growth. It called this supply-constrained, said customer forecasts point to its growth doubling next year, and said supply stays a bottleneck at least through the end of FY2028. It also reset the gross margin path: 74% in Q3, a Q4 trough of 71–72%, then 72–73% in FY2028 on memory costs.

The balance sheet has grown more complex since January. Supply and capacity commitments rose to $279B from $119B a quarter earlier. Maximum guarantee exposure is $108.5B after the $105B SB Energy/OpenAI guarantees. Receivables are $63.1B (from $38.5B) and inventory is $31.6B (from $21.4B). Equity investments are $99B, with $25B of further commitments. Debt is $33.4B after a $25B June issue.

Market framing: the options-implied move is ±8.7%, against a ±4.0% average closing move over the last 8 reports. The price is $204.64 against a consensus target of $339.17. Shares rose 8.7% after the Q2 report.

since_filing.text: On 2026-09-02 NVIDIA agreed to acquire Hugging Face for about $11.9B plus up to about $1.0B of equity retention, expected to close in 1H 2027 subject to regulatory approvals. The 8-K adds a risk factor on government restrictions on open-source and China-origin models.

NVIDIA committed $3B to Meta's equity offering (Meta is raising up to $95B). Meta also plans to deploy more NVIDIA infrastructure, including Vera Rubin and Vera CPUs. This adds to ecosystem equity exposure on top of the $99B of investments and $25B of commitments at Jul 26.

The New York Times reported on Oct 29 that US intelligence believes a Chinese national who led NVIDIA customer Megaspeed and has a relationship with Jensen Huang passed information to Beijing. NBC has not independently confirmed the details. This is a headline and China-policy risk, with no direct change to the guide.

Seaport reiterated Sell on Oct 23, saying competitive pressures are 'mounting' and reading NVIDIA's 'aggressive finance bundling' as a reaction to competition. Seaport also said it could be wrong in the coming months.

Late-October market backdrop: Alphabet fell about 12% on Oct 29, its steepest drop since its 2004 IPO, as Google's earnings reignited AI jitters and the Nasdaq led indexes lower. Amazon's trailing free cash flow was reported at a record outflow of more than $42B as AI spending more than doubled. Anthropic filed for an IPO.

Peer filings show vendor-linked financing spreading. Broadcom's AI XPV platform has a $35B initial tranche with a backstop of up to about $29B, and Broadcom says top customers are pressing for leasing and deferred-payment terms. AMD reports Data Center revenue of $6.7B (+107% YoY) and warns of customer financing needs and rising memory prices. These are proxy signals from earlier quarters, not NVIDIA data.

Contradiction flag: the call and the 10-Q (both 2026-08-26) differ in two places. The call said NVIDIA would provide credit enhancement for nearly 2 GW for another lab, but the 10-Q guarantee table shows only the $3.5B AI-cloud and $105B SB Energy guarantees. The call also cited a 'SoftBank Energy' 'Portsmouth' campus where the 10-Q says SB Energy Corp.'s PORTS campus in Pike County, Ohio. The 10-Q wording governs, and the 2 GW support is unquantified in the filings.

key_debates.question: Can Q3 clear a consensus that already sits above the top of guidance?

bull.text: NVIDIA has beaten 4 of 4 recent quarters by an average of 3.4%, and demand is described as far above supply, with Rubin ramping and Meta and AWS expanding deployments.

bear.text: Consensus revenue of $111.36B is above the $110.2B top of the guided range. The options market implies ±8.7% against a ±4.0% average move, and the stock rose 8.7% after Q2, so a modest beat may not be rewarded.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q3 revenue relative to about $111B, and the Q4 revenue guide relative to expectations, since the FY28 70% framework raises the bar for sequential growth.

key_debates.question: How deep and how long is the gross margin trough?

bull.text: Management has bracketed the path: 74% in Q3, a 71–72% trough in Q4, then 72–73% in FY28 once executed price increases take effect in Q1. Q2 gross margin was 75.0%, roughly flat with 74.9% in Q1.

bear.text: Memory pricing has exceeded prior expectations and is 'headed even higher into next year'. AMD also flags rising memory prices, and $279B of supply commitments are mostly memory and manufacturing capacity, so cost risk may outrun price increases.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The Q3 gross margin print versus 74% ±50bp, and whether the Q4 guide stays in 71–72% or moves lower.

key_debates.question: Is ecosystem financing building concentrated, circular risk?

bull.text: Management says compute is consumed by investment-grade customers or those backed by one, the platform is fungible and redeployable, and NVIDIA's risk is limited. Investments of nearly $50B in frontier labs are small against expected free cash flow.

bear.text: Guarantee exposure is up to $108.5B, supply commitments are $279B, and receivables rose to $63.1B on extended terms. The 10-K said NVIDIA had not entered into financing arrangements, but the 10-Q now says such arrangements affect cash flow timing. Seaport calls this finance bundling a response to competition.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The next 10-Q: the commitments and guarantees table, receivables and DSO, any new guarantees or purchase commitments, and non-marketable investment marks.

key_debates.question: Is the ~70% FY28 growth framework durable against competition and AI-spend skepticism?

bull.text: Management says demand is much greater than supply, the top-5 hyperscalers' capex is expected near $1.3T in 2027 and AWS is adding 2M GPUs starting this quarter through Q2 FY29. These external figures are management-cited and unverified.

bear.text: Broadcom is building financed custom-XPU capacity with a target above 20 GW through 2028 for frontier labs, Alphabet's 12% fall reignited AI-spending jitters, and Amazon's free cash flow is at a record outflow.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The tone of the Q4 outlook, any update to the FY28 framework, customer capex commentary through year-end, and ACIE growth versus Hyperscale.

claim.text: Commitments, guarantees and financing: supply commitments of $279B, total commitments of $366B and guarantee exposure of $108.5B, with a new 10-Q risk factor. NVIDIA warns it may be unable to reduce commitments if demand differs, and has agreed to buy unsold AI-cloud capacity.

Customer concentration and credit: one direct customer was 16% of Q2 revenue and five customers are 10–22% of receivables each. Extended terms of 90 days to one year raise credit and cash-timing risk, and an AI research company is a meaningful indirect customer.

Memory costs and gross margin: memory price increases exceeded prior expectations and the margin is guided to a 71–72% trough in Q4. Rubin ramp complexity could add provisions, warranty and yield costs.

Earnings quality: equity-security gains of $7.77B in Q2 and $23.7B in H1 inflate GAAP EPS, and the portfolio is concentrated, with $36.9B of public holdings under lock-up and $51.2B of private holdings valued on observable-price adjustments.

China and geopolitics: NVIDIA is effectively foreclosed from China data center compute, H200 sales are under 1% of Data Center revenue with an unrecoverable 25% tariff, and a preliminary China antitrust finding on Mellanox remains unresolved. The Oct 29 NYT report adds headline risk around a customer linked to Chinese intelligence.

Competition and bundled financing: custom-accelerator rivals are offering financed capacity, with a Broadcom backstop of about $29B and customers pressing for leasing and deferred payment. AMD cites NVIDIA's market position as a pricing constraint.

Acquisition and regulatory risk from the Hugging Face deal (about $11.9B plus up to $1.0B retention): closing needs regulatory approvals, and the 8-K flags that restrictions on open or China-origin models could materially hit the platform.

questions_for_management.question: What is the total ecosystem exposure over the next several years (equity, guarantees, purchase commitments), and how much is cash in FY28?

why.text: On the call, an analyst summed the commitments to about $500B and asked for the total and the FY28 cash portion. Management answered only on supply commitments, so no total or cash figure was given.

questions_for_management.question: What is the status, size and form of the credit enhancement for nearly 2 GW for another frontier lab, and why is it not in the guarantee table?

why.text: The call mentioned this support, but the 10-Q's $108.5B guarantee table lists only the AI-cloud and SB Energy guarantees.

questions_for_management.question: What is behind the rise in receivables and DSO, and what are the terms and concentration of the extended-payment deals? Are any of them effectively financing?

why.text: Receivables rose to $63.1B and DSO to 60 days on extended terms of up to a year. The call said 'we're not making loans', while the 10-K said NVIDIA had not entered financing arrangements and the 10-Q now says such arrangements affect cash flows.

questions_for_management.question: How should we split the roughly 70% FY28 growth among pricing, Rubin content, CPUs, Groq and volume, and what would the unconstrained number be?

why.text: Rasgon asked for this split and for the unconstrained number. Huang said only that it would be 'a lot higher', and the price increases take effect in Q1.

questions_for_management.question: What is the cost path for memory beyond Q4, and how much of the Q4 margin trough is mix, memory or Rubin ramp costs? How much will price increases recover?

why.text: Management reset gross margin to a 71–72% trough in Q4, citing memory costs that are 'headed even higher', while the 10-Q was silent on forward margin pressure.

questions_for_management.question: How do the revenue-share and take-or-pay structures with AI clouds affect revenue recognition, and what is NVIDIA's maximum purchase obligation if AI clouds cannot sell the capacity?

why.text: The call described a structure in which NVIDIA 'gets paid twice', but the 10-Q says AI clouds can stop providing capacity and sell it elsewhere at better rates, and that NVIDIA agreed to buy unsold capacity. The commitments total $36B.

questions_for_management.question: Does the Meta equity commitment and other recent investments change your equity-commitment total, and how should we think about future mark-to-market gains in Other income?

why.text: Equity investments were $99B and equity investment commitments $25B at Jul 26. Q2 other income included $7.77B of equity-security gains, which the 10-Q says were primarily unrealized. NVIDIA committed a further $3B to Meta's equity offering in October.

data_gaps: Q3 consensus EPS of $2.53 comes without any indication of whether it is GAAP or non-GAAP, so comparison to the $2.46 GAAP and $2.22 adjusted Q2 EPS is uncertain.
No whisper EPS is available: the next report is 17 days away and the whisper lookup runs automatically within 3 days.
No consensus figures for gross margin, opex, Data Center segment revenue or the Q4 outlook were found, so margin and mix expectations cannot be compared to the Street.

The Q2 revenue and margin guide from the prior quarter's press release is dated outside the 14-day window, so the beat-versus-guide pattern cannot be cited here. Only the 4-for-4 beat record against consensus is available.

Management's '60% of free cash flow returned' does not reconcile to filing data (H1 buybacks of $39.0B plus dividends of $6.3B against derived free cash flow of about $70B, roughly 65%), probably because of a different free cash flow definition.
No in-window competitor news on AMD pricing, margins or accelerator shipments was found. The AMD and Broadcom read-across rests on filings from the June–July quarters.

No in-window sell-side notes on the Q3 setup were found beyond Seaport's Sell. BNP Paribas's raise of its target to $345 (Oct 5) and Hugging Face-related notes (September) are outside the 14-day window and are background only.
The sources do not quantify the size, form or timing of the credit enhancement for nearly 2 GW for another frontier lab that was mentioned on the call.

The filings do not verify management-cited external demand figures (cloud backlog above $2T, hyperscaler capex of about $800B in 2026 and $1.3T in 2027, AI VC funding above $400B, and the sub-one-year ROIC that Huang said he 'heard').
